title: Partition identities
key_idea: An **integer partition** of $n$ is a weakly decreasing sequence $\lambda_1 \geq \lambda_2 \geq \cdots \geq \lambda_k > 0$ with $\sum \lambda_i = n$. The OGF is $\sum_n p(n)x^n = \prod_{k \geq 1} 1/(1-x^k)$. Classical identities (Euler, Jacobi, Rogers–Ramanujan) equate different partition families; many have elegant bijective proofs via Young diagrams or Ferrers diagrams.
summary: **To be filled in when you reach this section.** Key results: Euler's partition theorem (odd parts = distinct parts), conjugation of partitions (Young diagram transpose), Ferrers diagrams, the Jacobi triple product, generating functions with restrictions (distinct parts, bounded parts), and a taste of Rogers-Ramanujan.

notation.description: Number of partitions of $n$ into at most $k$ parts (equivalently, parts $\leq k$)
